title: hotfix: prevent SLO-enforcer split-brain during concurrent regional failover
author: Alex Nguyen
description: Motivation: customers observed brief correctness/latency regressions during cross-region failovers that correlated with the SLO-enforcer performing simultaneous backoff + failover transitions in two regions (a split-brain). Root cause: a race in regional failover path where instance-local in-memory circuit-breaker state and persistent coordinator state could diverge during concurrent epoch transitions. This allowed two regions to both accept traffic briefly which violated our capacity assumptions and caused downstream latency spikes. This hotfix ensures atomicity between coordinator state transitions and local in-memory enforcer state, adds quorum checks to prevent dual-primary scenarios, and tightens hysteresis/backoff ordering to avoid oscillation.
commits: fix(slo-enforcer): add coordinator-driven transition lock and quorum guard
chore(test): add unit + integration tests for concurrent failover paths
fix(cb): make circuit-breaker state transitions idempotent and persist tombstones
perf: reduce timer drift by aligning backoff windows to coordinator epoch
changed_snippets: services/slo_enforcer/manager.go: wrap region transition in Coordinator.BeginTransition(epoch) / Coordinator.CommitTransition(epoch) to ensure atomic updates
pkg/circuitbreaker/cb_store.go: persist tombstone on OPEN -> CLOSED transition to prevent stale leaders from re-opening
pkg/coordinator/raft_sync.go: add quorum check before marking region as primary; expose epoch ID in transition messages
tests/integration/slo_failover_concurrency_test.go: simulate concurrent failover from two regions and assert single-primary invariant

root_cause_summary: Race between local in-memory CB map updates and coordinator epoch transitions allowed two regions to both consider themselves primary during near-simultaneous failovers. The in-memory path didn't consult persisted tombstones or current coordinator epoch atomically.
fix_summary: 1) Introduce Coordinator transition API that obtains a distributed transition lock and publishes epoch IDs. 2) Add quorum guard before marking a region primary. 3) Make circuit-breaker state transitions idempotent and persist tombstones on OPEN->CLOSED. 4) Add unit and integration tests reproducing the race. 5) Adjust hysteresis/backoff ordering to avoid oscillation.
risk_and_mitigation: Low: code paths are exercised by unit+integration tests and a short canary in us-west-2. Mitigations: feature-gated rollouts, short TTL tombstones, and conservative default hysteresis (configurable).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge to main via squash. 2) Canary to us-west-2 (small % of traffic) for 2 hours. 3) Gradual roll out to other regions over 4 hours if no regressions. 4) Emergency rollback path by toggling slo-enforcer.failover_coordinator.enabled=false.
release_notes: Fixes a race during concurrent regional failovers that could briefly allow two regions to accept traffic (split-brain) causing SLO violations. Adds stronger coordinator-guarded transitions and persistent tombstones to the SLO enforcer.
merge_details: merged by Priya Shah using squash merge. Commit message summarizes fix + test coverage. CI green at time of merge.
